accueil.description: Discover James Bridle's Citizen Ex and create your digital passport: where does your data live and which laws apply to you?

citizen.titre: Citizen Ex – On the web, your citizenship no longer exists
citizen.description: On the web, your citizenship no longer exists. Discover Citizen Ex, James Bridle's artwork on the nationality of our data.

citizen.titre: On the web, your citizenship no longer exists.
citizen.paragraphe: Belonging to a nation is what gives us our rights and ensures our protection. When we browse the web, we have no defined nationality. It is common for the sites we use in one country to actually be hosted on the other side of the world.

passeport.intro: On the internet, you don't have just one nationality. Pick the sites you use: we'll show you where your data lives and which laws apply to you.
passeport.sites_aria: Sites to add to your passport

physique.description: The countries where your data is stored.

juridique.description: The countries whose law can reach your data.

score.phrase_aucun: Pick some sites to see your rights change.
score.phrase_90: Your data mostly stays under European law.
score.phrase_60: Foreign laws are starting to apply to you.
score.phrase_30: You depend heavily on foreign laws.
score.phrase_0: Most of your data falls under foreign laws.
score.aucune_perte: No rights lost with these sites.

dossier.vide: Tap a site to see its file.

passeport.avertissement: Educational simulation: the penalties are simplified estimates and do not constitute legal analysis.

BE.explication: Your data is protected by the GDPR and Belgian law.

FR.explication: Your data is protected by the GDPR and French law.

DE.explication: Your data is protected by the GDPR and German law.

IE.explication: Your data is protected by the GDPR, as applied in Ireland.

SG.explication: Physical hosting country only: none of the listed brands is legally tied to it.

US.explication: A US company can be forced to hand data over to US authorities, even if it is stored in Europe.

CN.explication: Chinese companies can be required to cooperate with their country's intelligence services.

google.message: Your query is processed close to home, in Belgium, but the company remains subject to US law.

youtube.message: Videos are delivered from servers close to your internet provider, but the platform is subject to US law.

instagram.message: Your data is managed from Ireland, but the parent company is American and subject to US law.

rtbf.message: Belgian public service: strong privacy protection under European law.

aliexpress.message: Your data travels through Singapore and Frankfurt, but the company is subject to Chinese law.

temu.message: Double exposure: the company is subject to Chinese law and its servers are with American hosting providers.

zalando.message: German company with servers in Germany, but the host is American: US law may apply.

netflix.message: Films are streamed from servers installed at Belgian internet providers, but the platform is subject to US law.

lesoir.message: Belgian media hosted locally: privacy protected under European law.

lemonde.hebergeur: To be verified (hosting in France assumed)
lemonde.message: French media hosted in France: privacy protected under European law.

decathlon.hebergeur: To be verified (centralised platform in France assumed)
decathlon.message: French company with an e-commerce platform centralised in France: protected under European law.
